We tell you what we tried and ask for screenshots, a screen recording or the steps your customer took. If the cause is an outside system, such as a payment gateway, we explain who to contact and what to tell them.
Do you fix problems caused by apps?

Checkout on Shopify is limited by the plan you are on, so we fix what the platform lets us change: shipping and tax rules, discount settings, payment methods and scripts. We test with real test orders.

desc:
Shopify store fixes for bugs and broken links means finding what is wrong in your store and repairing it properly. Ecom Swift LLC reproduces each problem, finds the cause, fixes it on a duplicate theme where code is involved and tests again before anything goes live.

## What are Shopify store fixes?

Shopify store fixes are targeted repairs to things that do not work as they should. Typical examples are links that lead to a 404 page, buttons that do nothing, images that fail to load, forms that never send, and checkout steps that show the wrong shipping or tax.

You can give us a list of problems you have noticed, or ask us to look for them. In both cases we explain the cause in plain words, so you know why it happened.

## Why small bugs cost real sales

Shoppers rarely report a broken button. They simply leave. A dead add-to-cart button, a menu that will not open on a phone or a contact form that sends nothing quietly turns visitors away, and you may not notice for weeks.

Problems at checkout are the most expensive. A shipping rate that is wrong, a tax line that looks odd or a payment step that fails can lose an order at the last moment. Broken links also confuse search engines and frustrate people who followed an old link from an email or social post.

## How careful fixing protects your store

A reliable repair starts with reproducing the problem. Until we can see it happen, we are guessing. Once we understand the cause, we can fix the source instead of hiding the symptom. A fix that only covers a symptom often returns after the next theme or app update.

Testing is the second half. We check the fix on phone and desktop, in the browser console where relevant, and with real test orders where checkout is involved. A safe process also protects your design: code changes are made on a duplicate theme, so your live store keeps working while we repair.

## What a good fix job includes

- A written list of issues, with how to see each one.
- Reproduction of every problem on phone and desktop.
- A plain explanation of the cause.
- A scan for broken links and 404 pages, with redirects to fitting pages.
- Fixes to buttons, menus, sections and layout glitches.
- Checks of forms and the notification emails they trigger.
- Test orders through checkout to check shipping, tax and totals.
- Review of console errors and theme code for deeper problems.
- Checks of payment and shipping rules.
- Short fix notes you can keep for later.

## What we do

We begin by confirming your list and adding anything we notice on a first walk through the store. For each item we write the steps that show the problem, so we are sure we are fixing the right thing.

Next, we find the cause. It might be a theme setting, a piece of code, a link that was never updated or an app that interferes with a page. Code changes go onto a duplicate theme and are tested before they replace the live version. The Basic package fixes a short list. Standard adds a wider bug sweep, redirects and test orders. Premium covers more issues, reviews code and rules in depth and includes a set of follow-up checks on the fixed items. If a problem comes from an app, we explain what we found and what options exist.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe each issue with the page address, the device and what you expected to happen.
- Send screenshots or a short screen recording if you can.
- Tell us when the problem started, or what changed just before.
- Keep a record of fixes so you can spot repeat problems.
- Test the store on your own phone after we finish.

**Avoid:**
- Editing theme code live while a fix is in progress.
- Installing a new app as a quick patch for a bug you do not understand.
- Reporting several problems as one vague complaint.
- Deleting pages that other pages still link to.
- Ignoring a checkout error because it only happens sometimes.

## Who this is for

This service suits owners with a list of small annoyances that never reach the top of the to-do list. It suits stores that changed themes or apps recently and now see odd behavior, and sellers who want a check before a big campaign. If customers have told you that something does not work, this is the right place to start.

## What we need from you

We need a collaborator or staff invitation and your list of issues, with screenshots where possible. We never need your password. If we cannot reproduce a problem, we tell you what we tried and what we need to continue, such as the device or steps you used. You own all changes in your own store, and each fix is explained in writing.
